status_note: Block 1 of a 3-block engine transformation arc. Block 2 (volume expansion, 8-12 weeks) and Block 3 (polarised, 12-16 weeks) ship as separate program.json files. Block 1 covers weeks 1-8: build a base you can actually train on top of. Dates in phases[] are template anchors starting from a canonical Mon 2026-01-05; the generator remaps them to the user's real start date on activation.

goals.primary_intent: Build a durable aerobic engine. Block 1 is the base — Z1/Z2 volume with a single hard weekly stimulus once the base is laid. This is the foundation the next two blocks build on.

arc.block_1_base: 8 weeks — this program. Aerobic base, first exposure to threshold and VO2max work in weeks 4-7, retest week 8.
arc.block_2_volume: 8-12 weeks — where the majority of VO2max gains land. Two hard sessions per week, higher Z1/Z2 volume, longer intervals.
arc.block_3_polarise: 12-16 weeks — advanced. 80/20 polarised model, race-specific work, taper and test.
arc.note: The three blocks compound. Block 1 in isolation moves the needle 5-8% on VO2max and drops resting HR meaningfully. Full engine transformation is a 6-month project across all three blocks.

block_1_targets.note: Expected ranges for a beginner-to-intermediate user completing weeks 1-8 as prescribed. Advanced users at the top of the aerobic ladder will see smaller gains in Block 1 and larger ones in Block 3.

modality_policy.weeks_1_to_4: Low-impact only — row, bike, or ski-erg. No running. Reason: capillary and mitochondrial adaptation lags connective-tissue tolerance by weeks. Running in weeks 1-4 raises injury risk without accelerating aerobic gains.
modality_policy.weeks_5_to_8: If the user's declared goal modality (from intake) is running, running is introduced in week 5, one session at a time, replacing a Z1 session first. Otherwise stay on the declared low-impact modality throughout.
modality_policy.cross_modal: Users who declared row/bike/ski-erg as their goal can substitute a Z1 session on a different modality if their preferred machine is unavailable. Hard sessions stay on the declared modality.

rules: 2-3 strength sessions per week, no more.
RPE cap of 7. No PR attempts, no top-set AMRAPs, no failure.
6+ hours separation from any hard cardio session on the same day.
If both must share a day, do the strength session first (fatigue transfers less that way).
If in doubt, skip the strength session on Norwegian 4x4 days.
concurrent_strength_policy.rationale: Hickson (1980) showed strength gains are attenuated by concurrent endurance training in proportion to endurance volume. Wilson & Loenneke (2012) meta-analysis: interference is largest when endurance sessions are hard and frequent. Docherty & Sporer (2000) modelled the interference as competition for the same recovery substrate. Practical translation: an 8-week base block is not the block to chase a squat PR. Hold what you have, come back to it in Block 2 or later.
acceptable_lifts: Upper-body pressing / pulling at moderate load
not_this_block: Smolov Jr or any high-frequency squat block
Metcons that generate systemic fatigue lasting into the next cardio day

principles.rule: Most volume easy, small amount hard, almost nothing in between
principles.detail: Seiler's polarised model (2010) is the backbone. In Block 1 you don't have enough volume yet to fully polarise — but the shape starts here. As blocks 2 and 3 add volume the 80/20 ratio locks in.

principles.rule: Weeks 1-2 are pure Z1. No exceptions.
principles.detail: You are laying capillary bed and mitochondrial density. Hard intervals on a base that isn't there yet just generate fatigue without adaptation. This is the most common mistake in DIY engine work.

principles.rule: One hard session per week in Block 1. That's it.
principles.detail: Second hard session lands in Block 2 once the base can absorb it. Push tier optionally adds a second by week 6-7 for users who came in with existing aerobic capacity.

principles.rule: Running enters at week 5 at earliest and only for run-goal users
principles.detail: Tendon and bone loading adapt slower than the cardiovascular system. Row/bike/ski for the first four weeks regardless of long-term goal.

principles.rule: Every retest metric that can be measured gets measured
principles.detail: Rest HR + submax HR at fixed pace are always available. 500m row TT and 1km run TT depend on user setup. Whichever you can do gives partial credit. The delta tells you whether Block 1 worked.

questions.label: Realistically, how many days per week can you commit?
questions.help: Honest answer wins. If your ceiling is 2, we'll tell you upfront whether this program can deliver on its claim at that dose.

questions.label: How many hours of cardio (running, rowing, cycling, ski-erg, hiking that raised HR meaningfully) have you done per week, averaged over the last 3 months?
questions.help: Only count sessions where HR was elevated for 20+ minutes continuously. CrossFit metcons and Hyrox stations don't count unless HR stayed up for the whole workout.

questions.help: 'HR runaway' means HR climbs 15+ bpm over the last 10 minutes at the same pace. If you're not sure, mark no.

questions.help: One session. Not accumulated. If you haven't done any, enter 0.

questions.label: Any joint or tendon issues that flare with cardio? Describe briefly.
questions.help: Knees, Achilles, hips, lower back. Free text — the plan doesn't gate on this field, but it's shown to you before hard sessions as a reminder to self-monitor.

questions.help: Read the concurrent-strength policy on the program page — 2-3 maintenance-only sessions is the recommendation.

questions.help: If not, you'll measure it on 3 mornings during the intake week and take the average.

physical_tests.label: Resting heart rate — morning average
physical_tests.instructions: For 3 mornings in the intake week, before getting out of bed and before caffeine, measure HR for 60 seconds (or use a wearable's overnight low). Record the average of the 3 readings. This is the single most sensitive early indicator of aerobic adaptation.

physical_tests.label: 5-minute submax HR at chosen easy pace
physical_tests.instructions: On your goal modality (row/bike/ski/run), warm up 5 min, then hold a comfortable, sustainable, conversational pace for exactly 5 minutes. Record HR at the end of the 5 minutes. This same pace will be used at retest — write it down (watts, split, or pace).

physical_tests.label: 500m row time trial — optional
physical_tests.instructions: Only if you have access to a rower. Warm up 10 min. Row 500m as fast as you can sustain. Record time in seconds. Skip if goal modality is not rowing and you don't want the second data point.

physical_tests.label: 1km run time trial — optional
physical_tests.instructions: Only if goal modality is running AND joints allow it. Warm up 10 min including 2 x 30s pickups. Run 1km hard on a flat track or GPS-measured route. Record time in seconds. Skip if goal modality is not running.

consent.label: I understand this is a training template, not medical advice. I'll consult a clinician for any joint issue that worsens under load, chest pain, or unexplained shortness of breath.
I consent to storing my logged symptoms and training metrics locally in this app. Data stays on my device / account and isn't shared.

safety_gates.block_body: The Norwegian 4x4 sessions push HR near max. Unmanaged hypertension makes that unsafe. Get BP treated before starting.
HR-based zones are unreliable during first-trimester pregnancy. Work with a specialist to adapt cardio prescription.
History of exertional syncope or unexplained cardiac symptoms is a full-clearance prerequisite before any high-intensity program.

safety_gates.block_title: Wait for baseline HR to normalise
safety_gates.block_body: Persistent HR elevation post-COVID means the cardiovascular system is still recovering. Interval work now can prolong recovery. Return when resting HR is back to baseline.
A flaring joint or tendon condition means don't add the running variant of intervals in week 5. Consider the cycling/rowing/erg version — or wait until the flare is resolved.

plan_tiers.label: Foundation
plan_tiers.typical_outcome: By week 8: comfortable holding 60 minutes of Z1 continuously. Resting HR drop of 3-8 bpm. Submax HR at your intake pace 3-6 bpm lower. VO2max improvement modest in Block 1 (~3-6%) — the transformation lands in Blocks 2 and 3 once the base is in.

program_adjustments.note: Foundation tier gets one fewer Z1 session per week versus Progression, and the first Norwegian 4x4 lands in week 5 (not week 4). Threshold cruise is introduced in week 6 instead of week 5. The whole ladder is shifted by one week and the last two weeks compress.

plan_tiers.label: Progression
plan_tiers.typical_outcome: By week 8: comfortable at 75-90 minute Z1 sessions. Resting HR drop of 5-10 bpm. Submax HR 5-10 bpm lower at the intake pace, or same HR at a faster pace. VO2max improvement 5-8% in Block 1. This is where most non-endurance-trained CrossFit / strength users start.

program_adjustments.note: Progression is the reference plan. Weekly template runs as written.

plan_tiers.label: Push
plan_tiers.typical_outcome: By week 8: 90+ minute Z1 sessions comfortable, threshold pace clearly established, Norwegian 4x4 hitting the top HR zone consistently. Resting HR drop of 5-10 bpm (smaller absolute drop because you started lower). VO2max improvement 4-7% (ceiling effect). Bigger gains come in Block 3's polarised phase.

program_adjustments.note: Push scales Z1 durations by ~15%, introduces Norwegian 4x4 in week 2 (after one baseline Z1 week), and adds a second weekly hard session from week 6. Retest week is the same.

phases.name: Week 1 — pure Z1 introduction
phases.goal: Two Z1 sessions of 45 minutes each. No intervals. If HR runs away, back off pace immediately.
phases.template_note: Push tier: same shape, but sessions run 50-55 min. Foundation: one session at 40 min if 45 is too much.
notes: This week is measurement plus habit-formation. If it feels laughably easy, you're on target.

phases.name: Week 2 — Z1 volume up
phases.goal: Three Z1 sessions, 40-45 minutes each. Push tier: introduces first Norwegian 4x4 in place of one Z1.
phases.template_note: Foundation tier: 2 Z1 sessions, 40-45 min each — hold volume rather than adding a third.

phases.name: Week 3 — first sustained tempo
phases.goal: Two Z1 (50-55 min) + one 20-minute sustained tempo. First taste of sub-threshold work.
phases.template_note: Foundation: skip the tempo — third Z1 session at 40 min instead.

phases.name: Week 4 — first Norwegian 4x4
phases.goal: One long Z1 (60 min) + one moderate Z1 (45 min) + first Norwegian 4x4 for Progression and Push tiers.
phases.template_note: Foundation tier: replace the 4x4 with a second sustained tempo (25 min). First 4x4 lands in week 5.
notes: The 4x4 costs more recovery than any other session in Block 1. Do not stack it with a hard strength session in the same 24 h window.
If HR won't climb to 90% max on set 1, you're too tired — reschedule and do Z1 instead.

phases.name: Week 5 — threshold enters + run-modality unlock
phases.goal: One long Z1 (75 min) + one 3×8 threshold + one 45-min Z1. If goal modality is running, running is introduced now — one Z1 session becomes a Z1 easy run.
phases.template_note: Push tier: threshold set becomes 3×10 minutes. Foundation: first 4x4 lands this week (delayed one week), no threshold this block.

phases.name: Week 6 — volume peaks, first 4-session week
phases.goal: Long Z1 (60) + moderate Z1 (45) + Norwegian 4x4 + easy recovery (30). This is the highest-volume week of Block 1.
phases.template_note: Push tier: adds a second hard session — swap the recovery for a sustained tempo (30 min). Foundation: 3 sessions total, drop the recovery.

phases.name: Week 7 — combined stimulus
phases.goal: Long Z1 (75) + sustained tempo (30) + Norwegian 4x4 + Z1 (40). Peak stimulus before deload.
phases.template_note: Foundation: threshold cruise instead of the 4x4 (3×8). Push tier as written; already at high load.

phases.name: Week 8 — deload and retest
phases.goal: One easy Z1 (60) early week, RETEST midweek, one very easy Z1 (40) after. Retest all metrics you measured at intake.
phases.test_at_end: Retest same protocol as intake: resting HR (record 3 mornings), 5-min submax HR at intake pace, 500m row TT if applicable, 1km run TT if applicable. Delta is the Block 1 outcome.
phases.template_note: All tiers do the same deload + retest. This is the honest measurement of what Block 1 did.
notes: Retest wants at least 48 h from any hard session and 24 h from any strength session.
Rest HR + submax HR are always measurable. Don't skip Block 2 just because a TT wasn't possible.

blocks.name: Zone 1/2 steady-state
blocks.note: Modality chosen at intake. Weeks 1-4 low-impact only (row/bike/ski). Running unlocks in week 5 for run-goal users. Session length varies by week and tier — see phase week_by_week / weekly_template.

items.scheme: See weekly template for duration by week and tier.

blocks.name: Sustained tempo — sub-threshold cruise
blocks.note: 10-12 min warm up including 2 x 30s pickups → hold sub-threshold pace for the target block → 5 min cool down. Sub-threshold = comfortably hard but sustainable, 83-88% VDOT / 88-94% FTP / 82-87% HRmax.

items.scheme: Week 3: 20 min. Week 7: 30 min. Push tier week 6 add-in: 30 min.

blocks.name: Threshold cruise intervals
blocks.note: 12-15 min warm up including 3 x 30s pickups → interval set → 5-8 min cool down. Intervals at lactate-threshold pace (85-90% HRmax).

items.scheme: Progression tier week 5: 3 x 8 min with 2 min recovery. Push tier week 5: 3 x 10 min. Foundation tier week 7 substitute: 3 x 8 min.

blocks.name: Norwegian 4x4 VO2max intervals
blocks.note: 12-15 min warm up including 3 x 30s pickups → 4 x [4 min @ 90-95% HRmax / 3 min active recovery] → 8-10 min cool down. The single hardest session in Block 1.

items.scheme: 4 sets × 4 min at 90-95% HRmax, 3 min active recovery between. Non-negotiable: full recovery day either side.

substitutions.if_hr_won't_climb_on_set_1: Bail out, switch to Z1 easy for 30 min. Reschedule the 4x4 with 48 h clear.
substitutions.if_joint_flares_at_running_4x4: Move the 4x4 back to the low-impact modality even if goal is running. Running-specific VO2max work belongs in Block 2.

blocks.name: Easy recovery flush
blocks.note: Very easy pace on any modality, HR under 65% max. Purpose is blood flow and recovery, not adaptation. Optional in Progression tier; only appears in week 6.

items.scheme: 30 minutes Z1 flush. If it feels like a workout, back off.

blocks.name: Block 1 retest
blocks.note: Repeat intake protocol. Log every metric you can measure. Rest HR and submax HR at the intake pace are always available.

items.scheme: See exercise instructions. Space time-trials by 15+ min of easy spin. Do not stack 500m row and 1km run in the same session unless goal is a combined engine — pick one.

weekly_template.note: Reference layout for Progression tier. Push adds a session; Foundation drops one. Sessions are meant to be placed on non-consecutive days when possible; 48 h between the hard session and the next hard session is non-negotiable.

optional_second_hard.placement: Wed or Fri, ≥6h from primary hard session, ≥48h from adjacent days

week_8.note: Retest is the point of week 8. Space it 48+ h from any hard session and 24+ h from strength.

placement_principles: Never place hard sessions on consecutive days.
48+ h between Norwegian 4x4 and any other hard session in the same week.
24+ h between a hard cardio session and any concurrent strength session; 6+ h if they must share a day.
If life forces you to skip a session, drop the last Z1 of the week — never the hard session. The hard stimulus is what moves the needle.
If you skip the hard session, do not double up next week. Move on.

progression_rules.assessment_note: Judge by next-morning HR variability and subjective recovery. Don't decide mid-session that you're 'not feeling it' — finish easy and reassess tomorrow.

states.label: Hold — swap a Z1 for scheduled hard session or shorten by 20%

conditions.or: life load 7+ or sleep < 6h two nights running

progression_rules.week_end_rule: If the week's hard session was hit at intended intensity and finished feeling like you had one more interval in the tank → proceed. If the hard session degraded across sets or HR wouldn't climb → hold at current volume next week; do not skip the deload/retest.
progression_rules.escalation: Two red days in the same week → skip the hard session that week. Three red days in a row, or any red day with unexplained resting HR elevation > 15 bpm, means take a full week off and consult a clinician if it persists.

daily_log_schema.derived_state_rule: red if morning_rhr > baseline + 10 OR new_joint_pain OR illness_symptoms; amber if rhr 5-10 above baseline OR life_load >= 7; else green

immediate_actions.action: Complete the intake questionnaire and physical tests within 5 days of starting.
immediate_actions.reason: Every retest metric requires an intake baseline to compare against. No baseline = no answer to 'did Block 1 work'.

immediate_actions.action: Buy or borrow a chest-strap HR monitor for the block if you don't have one.
immediate_actions.reason: Wrist-optical HR is fine for Z1 tracking but unreliable at the top end of Norwegian 4x4 sets. A chest strap costs less than a month of Netflix and makes the whole plan measurable.

immediate_actions.action: Decide the maintenance strength plan BEFORE week 1 and write down the 2-3 sessions you'll do each week.
immediate_actions.reason: The concurrent-training rules are non-negotiable, and 'I'll figure it out as I go' becomes 4-5 strength sessions creeping back in and the engine gains stalling.

immediate_actions.action: Set an appointment with yourself for Thursday of week 8 — the retest day. Put it in the calendar now.
immediate_actions.reason: Retest gets skipped when it's the last thing on a busy week. Book it like a meeting.

physiological_targets: Mitochondrial biogenesis via PGC-1α signalling — detectable at 5-10 training sessions, functional adaptation by 2-4 weeks, near-maximal for the given stimulus by 6-8 weeks (Little 2010, Perry 2010, Konopka 2014, Bishop 2019). Konopka 2014 measured β-HAD +397-435%, CS +65-102%, PGC-1α +55-62% in 12 weeks in older adults — no age blunting of relative response.

Capillary-to-fibre ratio +10-20% in 8 weeks; capillary density (per unit area) responds most reliably to endurance/continuous work (+13±3%), less to sprint-interval training (Andersen & Henriksson 1977; Cocks 2013; 2025 mito+cap meta-regression PMC11787188).

Left-ventricular stroke volume +5-10% in 8 weeks — REQUIRES interval intensity ≥90% HRmax. Z1 alone does not move SV meaningfully (Helgerud 2007: only the 4×4 and 15/15 groups showed SV gains, LSD and threshold groups did not). Cardiac remodelling is eccentric with endurance training (Baggish & Wood 2011).

Lactate clearance via MCT1 upregulation — training raises sarcolemmal MCT1 in oxidative tissue more reliably than MCT4. Endurance-trained subjects have higher MCT1 vs untrained (Pilegaard 2000; Brooks 2018 lactate shuttle theory). This is the specific adaptation that shortens between-interval recovery in metcons.
Resting HR −5 to −10 bpm in 8 weeks (12+ weeks: −10 to −15 bpm typical). Reflects parasympathetic tone + expanded stroke volume (multiple; Konopka 2014 as anchor).
Submax HR at fixed pace/power −8 to −15 bpm in 8 weeks. This moves FIRST and is the most motivating early metric — a training-effect signal visible before VO2max plateaus.
Fat oxidation rate at Fatmax (~63% VO2max in trained men, range 45-75%; Achten & Jeukendrup 2003). Z1 volume drives β-HAD and CPT1 upregulation — the enzymatic machinery for fat oxidation.

session_rationale.block_z1_steady: The single largest driver of mitochondrial + capillary adaptation across a 6-month arc. Konopka 2014: 12 weeks of 3-4×/week cycling at 60-80% HRR produced PGC-1α +55-62%, CS +65-102%, β-HAD +397-435%. Andersen & Henriksson 1977: 40 min/day × 4/wk × 8 wk at 80% VO2max drove capillary density +20% and VO2max +16%. San-Millán & Brooks 2018 identify Zone 2 as the intensity that recruits Type I fibres preferentially via the lactate-clamp methodology — the largest mitochondrial signal per unit of fatigue. Confidently the base-load session of the program.
session_rationale.block_sustained_tempo: Sub-threshold sustained work drives MCT1 upregulation (Pilegaard 2000) and shifts the crossover point toward higher intensities (Brooks & Mercier 1994). Jack Daniels' T-pace (~83-88% VDOT). Fills the missing middle: harder than Z1, easier than 4×4. The bridge session in weeks 3-5.
session_rationale.block_threshold_cruise: Longer intervals at ~85-90% HRmax. Rønnestad & Hansen 2020 comparison found SHORT intervals superior to long intervals for VO2max in trained cyclists — so we don't use threshold cruise to chase VO2max. What long intervals actually train is LT2 sustainable output: the pace/power that keeps improving after VO2max plateaus (Joyner & Coyle 2008). That's the specific job of this block.
session_rationale.block_norwegian_4x4: Helgerud 2007 (n=40): 4×4 min at 90-95% HRmax produced VO2max +7.2% and stroke volume +10% over 8 weeks — the only session type in that four-arm study that moved SV meaningfully. Wisløff 2007 (post-MI HF patients, 12 weeks): VO2peak +46%, LV ejection fraction +35% with the same 4×4 protocol. Time-at-VO2max is the specific driver of cardiac stroke-volume adaptation.
session_rationale.block_easy_recovery: Blood flow at Z1 (60-70% HRmax) accelerates lactate clearance and glycogen replenishment vs complete rest — active recovery. No adaptive stimulus intended. Appears in the peak-volume week where systemic fatigue rises and Wilson & Loenneke 2012 concurrent-training data indicate strength interference amplifies.
session_rationale.block_retest: Same protocol at intake and retest so the delta is trustworthy. Rest HR + submax HR at fixed pace are the two most sensitive early indicators of aerobic adaptation (both move faster than VO2max) and are equipment-independent. 500m row TT + 1km run TT add modality-specific measurements when equipment is available.

evidence_base.progression_rationale: Weeks 1-2 are pure Z1 because mitochondrial signalling protein bursts precede functional enzyme upregulation by 5-10 sessions (Perry 2010, Little 2010) — hard intervals on a missing base generate fatigue signals without adaptation payoff. First tempo lands week 3 as an MCT1 stimulus. First Norwegian 4×4 lands week 4 for Progression/Push tiers — Foundation delays hard work to week 5 because Ross 2015 showed non-response at low intensity converts to response at 75%, but pushing under-conditioned users straight into 4×4 amplifies dropout risk. Volume peaks weeks 6-7 with an added easy Z1 recovery session — Fyfe 2016 showed endurance VOLUME (not intensity) drives concurrent-training interference, so the peak-volume weeks are precisely where the strength cap tightens (RPE ≤ 6, no PR chasing). Week 8 deloads to a single easy Z1, retests midweek, and finishes easy — mirroring taper practice; Baar 2014's 3h AMPK-recovery window plus Robineau 2016's demonstrated 6h separation advantage inform the same-day sequencing rule (lift first if forced; 6+ h separation preferred; alternate days ideal).
evidence_base.outcome_evidence: Effect-size expectations synthesised across primary sources for a strength-trained user new to aerobic work. VO2max: Foundation tier +5-8%, Progression +8-12%, Push +2-5% (Push has less headroom). Anchor: Helgerud 2007 measured +7.2% at 3×/wk 4×4 in moderately trained subjects. Mitochondrial oxidative enzymes +40-100% (Konopka 2014, Perry 2010). Capillary-to-fibre ratio +10-20% (Andersen 1977, Cocks 2013). Stroke volume +5-10% if intervals present (Helgerud 2007). Resting HR −5 to −10 bpm by week 8 (visible from week 2-4). Submax HR at fixed pace −8 to −15 bpm (the fastest-moving, most motivating early metric). 500m row TT: 3-8s improvement, mostly from pacing + stroke efficiency, not raw physiology. 2km row or 1km run TT: 5-12% improvement — physiology + running/rowing economy. Individual variation is real: HERITAGE (Bouchard 1999) showed heritability of VO2max training response = 47% and ~10× range in individual gains under identical prescription. Ross 2015 showed ~18% of subjects were 'non-responders' at 50% intensity — non-response was substantially reduced at 75% intensity. Non-response is usually under-dosing, not genotype. Block 2 (volume expansion) and Block 3 (polarised specialisation) capture the majority of VO2max-available gains — Block 1 is the base that lets them work.

outcome_by_tier.dose_calibration_note: Block 1 (8 weeks) delivers 1 primary hard session per week in weeks 3-6, escalating to 2 hard sessions in week 7. This is a starter dose — Helgerud's +7.2% VO2max protocol used 3 hard sessions/wk × 8wk. Users targeting the upper end of the projected range should stack the optional second hard session (marked as such in Weeks 3-6 layout) with ≥6h from the primary. Full Blocks 2 and 3 (not shipped yet) are what complete the polarised arc.

contraindications: Unmanaged hypertension (BP > 160/100 at rest) — see a clinician before starting the Norwegian 4x4 sessions. Z1 work is generally safe but check.
First-trimester pregnancy — HR-based zones are unreliable during pregnancy; work with a specialist.
Any joint or tendon condition that flares under load (Achilles, patellar tendinopathy, hip labral tear on the run variant) — stay on low-impact modality; do not switch to running in week 5.
Post-COVID convalescence with persistent resting HR elevation or exercise intolerance — do not begin intervals until baseline HR normalises.
History of exertional syncope or unexplained cardiac symptoms — full clearance first.
evidence_base.adaptive_engine_hooks: Morning resting HR is the primary daily signal — >10 bpm above baseline gates the day's hard session to Z1 automatically (proposal, user Accepts). Two red days in a week gates the following hard session to a threshold cruise (lower cost than 4x4). Life-load score of 7+ mid-week combined with a missed session prompts a Z1 substitution on the hard day rather than a make-up. If the block's Norwegian 4x4 HR fails to reach 90% HRmax on set 1 twice in a row, engine proposes a threshold cruise substitute the following week and flags a review. If a hard aerobic session lands within 6 hours of a lifting session, engine proposes moving one or the other — Robineau 2016 dose-response showed 6+ h separation preserves both adaptations, 0h separation halves the strength gain. All adjustments respect the confirm-first rule — engine proposes, user Accepts, nothing mutates silently.
engineering_choices_flagged: Session length (45 vs 60 vs 75 min for Z1 steady) — no strong evidence at this granularity; picked to fit real-world weekly hours
Retest cadence at week 8 — engineering choice; matches the block boundary
Number of intervals per interval session (3 vs 4 vs 5) — coaching consensus, not directly RCT-tested
Recovery ratio for 4×4 (3 min at 60% HRmax) — Helgerud 2007 protocol, but exact ratio is not empirically optimised
The specific HRmax formula (211 − 0.64 × age from HUNT / Nes 2013) — has ~11 bpm SEE; personalised max derived from observed workout HRs when available

One hard session per week in Block 1 — Stöggl & Sperlich support polarised distribution but do not prescribe a single-session ceiling. Our engineering choice biased to strength-preservation in a concurrent-context user.

Sub-threshold tempo as MCT1 stimulus — Pilegaard 2000 measured MCT1 upregulation across a range of intensities; the sub-threshold framing is our engineering read of where the base-first stimulus fits the polarised model, not a paper-validated intensity anchor.

Push-tier week-2 4×4 introduction — Ross 2015 justifies 75% intensity over 50% but does not prescribe the specific week of introduction. Engineering choice biased to giving Push users an earlier hard-session signal.
evidence_base.hr_zone_methodology: Default: HRmax from HUNT formula (211 − 0.64 × age) per Nes 2013 — has 10.8 bpm standard error but no sex/BMI/fitness interaction. Zone floors set as %HRR (Karvonen 1957) rather than %HRmax because %HRR accounts for resting HR, which is itself the trained-fitness signal. Preferred: observed HRmax from a hard interval session, stored per-user, updated as fitness changes. Optional (chest-strap owners): DFA a1 = 0.75 as VT1 anchor per Rogers 2021 — validated in elite and recreational populations, non-invasive proxy for the aerobic threshold.
evidence_base.concurrent_strength_prescription: During the 8-week block, keep barbell strength at RPE ≤ 7 maintenance: 2-3 sessions/week, same lifts, same volume, no PR chasing. Schumann 2022 meta-analysis of 43 studies: maximal strength SMD = -0.06 (not significant), hypertrophy SMD = -0.01 (not significant), BUT explosive strength SMD = -0.28 (significant, meaningful). Chasing explosive PRs during aerobic emphasis is the specific loss zone. If same day is unavoidable, lift first (Eddens 2018 meta: +6.91% lower-body strength gain vs endurance-first). Minimum 6 h separation (Robineau 2016). Protein floor 1.6 g/kg/day (Morton 2018 meta). Fuel resistance sessions fully (Impey 2018 'Fuel for the Work Required').

onboarding_steps.title: The 0-10 scale
onboarding_steps.body_md: You'll rate how ready you feel most mornings and how heavy the day around training feels — simple scales, no jargon. Here's how the numbers read:

onboarding_steps.title: Life load, today
onboarding_steps.body_md: Sleep, work, stress, illness — anything that shows up before you get to the session. Terav uses this to propose a lighter target when it's high. Nothing else.

onboarding_steps.title: How Engine Builder works
onboarding_steps.body_md: Three sessions a week — one Zone 1-2 steady, one 4×4 interval, one skill / mobility. The other four days are yours. If you push hard elsewhere, log it in the morning check and the engine softens the next session. Progress is measured against the Zone-2 anchor pace, not RPE.

currently_reads.label: Per-set / per-interval RPE when you log it
Free-text notes for fatigue and external-load keywords

would_additionally_use.label: Heart rate at Zone-2 anchor
would_additionally_use.why_it_matters: Zone-2 pacing depends on cardiac drift over time — the same effort should hold the same HR. Without HR the engine can't see improvement week-to-week.
would_additionally_use.user_action_free: Log avg + peak HR after each Z1/Z2 session.
would_additionally_use.user_action_paid: Connect Garmin / Whoop / Apple Watch — HR auto-logs.

would_additionally_use.label: Weekly retest at the Zone-2 anchor
would_additionally_use.why_it_matters: Without a fixed anchor test, drift can't be measured across weeks. Retest = the ground truth the engine uses.
would_additionally_use.user_action_free: Do the weekly Zone-2 retest on its scheduled day.

variance_source.note: HERITAGE Family Study documented 47% heritability of VO2max training response and ~10× individual variance in gains under identical prescription. Ross 2015 clarified most 'non-response' at Foundation-tier intensities is actually under-dosing.

under_dosing.copy: Your mid-block submax HR looks flat AND your logged intensity is below 80% of prescribed. Not a genetic ceiling — you're under-dosed. The engine will propose a 4×4 slot in place of your next steady-state to lift the stimulus.

true_non_response.copy: You've hit prescribed intensity but the aerobic signals aren't moving. HERITAGE 10× variance in play. Options: (1) finish this block honestly, expect small Push-tier gains; (2) swap to Rowing 2K where task-specific coordination compensates; (3) accept genetic ceiling and move to maintenance.

responding.copy: Submax HR is trending down as expected. Keep the current prescription — the Week-8 retest will confirm the direction.

retest_metrics_mid_block.purpose: First of two HERITAGE-baseline points. Compare against Week-1 baseline to classify response direction before the end-block retest.
